title: Stochastic Recursive Inclusions under Biased Perturbations: An Input-to-State Stability Perspective
summary: This paper investigates the asymptotic behavior of stochastic recursive inclusions in the presence of non-zero, non-diminishing bias, a setting that frequently arises in zeroth-order optimization, stochastic approximation with iterate-dependent noise, and distributed learning with adversarial agents. The analysis is conducted through the lens of input-to-state stability of an associated differential inclusion, which serves as the continuous-time limit of the discrete recursion.
